body:
The cause is that HammerParent is a Hand-IK child, and there is a rotation exceeding the 180-degree boundary from bone rest in the Hand-IK animation. In other words, the problem is that you are trying to blend the global rotation directly, rather than using a step-by-step (characters joints) accumulated rotations.

As documented in https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/animation/animation_tree.html#for-better-blending, animation blending attempts to prevent character fractures by avoiding rotations that cross the 180-degree axis during blending. It means that the transition in the blend tree is only a transition of the blend amount (and result is accumulated by the amount from the 0 offset by rest), and does not directly interpolate between the two poses.

rest
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0546fc9c-385e-4854-aa2a-3a999653c062)

in jump animation (only enable Hand-IK track)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/45967c80-9520-4963-9234-278d4e205c95)

The most straightforward method currently available is to make HammerParent a child of Hand.

Or it would be possible to simply assign the BoneAttachment directly to the Hand and use the offset inside that Node, as shown in the modified MRP below.

[animation-bug-modified.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20548512/animation-bug-modified.zip)

When considering the reasons for this parent-child relationship, it may be that you want to rotate the hammer 180 degrees, but in that case, we recommend adding another bone to the child, or nesting a node within BoneAttachment, and playing the rotation animation outside of AnimationBlendTree using a separate AnimationPlayer (AnimationPlaybackTrack can probably be used for this). -This may be documented, but if necessary, I think a separate issue should be raised for documentation purposes with a track that rotates more than 180 degrees with including animations like baton twirling.

First of all, thank you for taking your time going over this issue and providing such a complete explanation, I would not have guessed what the problem was on my own.

Parenting `Hammer.Parent` to `Hand.R` solves the problem completely. I didn't intend to animate the hammer separately, so keeping the setup like this is perfect for now. 

I think the documentation link you shared is very complete about the requirements of interpolating animations. The problem here was me not understanding how Skeletons and bones work, so there is no need to open another issue.

Thanks again.
